$note: Display name and plain-language 'why it matters' line for each of the 19 rubric factors. Used for the heatmap header tooltips and the 'What the columns mean' legend (see skills/eb5-report/SKILL.md enhancement 4). Weights and scoring live in scoring-rubric.json.

I1.name: Regional Center good standing
I1.why: If the regional center is terminated or not approved for the project's state, every investor petition behind it is exposed.

I2.name: I-956F project approval
I2.why: The I-956F is the project's own approval. Until the regional center FILES it, no investor can even submit an I-526E.

I3.name: Job creation
I3.why: Fewer than 10 countable jobs per investor means the green card fails at I-829, however well the building performs.

I4.name: TEA / set-aside validity
I4.why: The set-aside is what buys the $800K price and the shorter queue. Rural is pure geography, so it can be checked independently.

I5.name: Sustainment (2-year at-risk)
I5.why: Capital must stay genuinely at risk for two years. If the loan repays too early, the petition is undermined.

I6.name: Redeployment
I6.why: If money comes back before I-829, it must be redeployed. Undisclosed terms mean the sponsor decides alone.

I7.name: Approval track record
I7.why: A sponsor that has actually carried investors through I-829 is evidence the process works end to end.

I8.name: Fund admin / audits / securities
I8.why: A fund administrator or annual audit is what stops investor money being moved without oversight.

I9.name: Source-of-funds integrity
I9.why: A weak source-of-funds record is the most common reason an otherwise sound petition is denied.

F1.name: Capital-stack position & EB-5 %
F1.why: Where EB-5 sits in the stack decides who absorbs the first loss. Senior over real equity is very different from senior over nothing.

F2.name: Loan vs equity & terms
F2.why: A secured loan with a defined maturity is materially safer for the investor than open-ended equity.

F3.name: Collateral & guarantees
F3.why: A guaranty smaller than the loan, or one that only guarantees completion rather than repayment, may not return the money.

F4.name: Developer balance sheet & litigation
F4.why: If the developer is insolvent, the building may finish but the loan may never be repaid.

F5.name: Construction / completion risk
F5.why: Unentitled or unpermitted projects can stall for years, which stops both the jobs and the repayment.

F6.name: Market / demand risk
F6.why: Weak demand shows up as low occupancy or slow sales, which is what actually breaks the refinance.

F7.name: Repayment / takeout source
F7.why: Every EB-5 loan needs something to repay it. No committed takeout means repayment is a hope, not a plan.

F8.name: Escrow & redeployment (financial)
F8.why: Escrow decides whether your money is released before or after the approvals you are relying on.

F9.name: Fees & conflicts
F9.why: Fees paid outside the offering do not appear in the headline $800,000 and directly reduce your net return.

F10.name: Return-of-capital history
F10.why: A sponsor that has actually returned capital before is the best available evidence you will get yours back.
